1.name: Pliocene marine rocks
1.lithology: Major: sandstone, mudstone; Minor: siltstone, claystone, conglomerate
1.description: Sandstone, siltstone, shale, and conglomerate; in part Pleistocene and Miocene.
1.reference: Saucedo, G.J., Bedford, D.R., Raines, G.L., Miller, R.J., and Wentworth, C.M., 2000, GIS Data for the Geologic Map of California, California Department of Conservation, Division of Mines and Geology, CD-ROM 2000-07, scale 1:750,000. 2.name: Quaternary alluvium and marine deposits
2.lithology: Major: coarse alluvium; Minor: fine alluvium
2.description: Alluvium, lake, playa, and terrace deposits; unconsolidated and semi-consolidated. Mostly nonmarine, but includes marine deposits near the coast.
2.reference: Saucedo, G.J., Bedford, D.R., Raines, G.L., Miller, R.J., and Wentworth, C.M., 2000, GIS Data for the Geologic Map of California, California Department of Conservation, Division of Mines and Geology, CD-ROM 2000-07, scale 1:750,000. 3.description: Upper Cretaceous sandstone, shale, and conglomerate

5.description: Extensive marine and nonmarine sand deposits, generally near the coast or desert playas

6.name: Franciscan Complex, unit 1 (Coast Ranges)
6.lithology: Major: sandstone, mudstone; Minor: chert; Incidental: limestone, conglomerate, greenstone, serpentinite, gabbro, amphibolite, schist, felsic volcanic
6.description: Franciscan complex: Cretaceous and Jurassic sandstone with smaller amounts of shale, chert, limestone, and conglomerate. Includes Franciscan melange, except where separated--see KJfm.
6.reference: Saucedo, G.J., Bedford, D.R., Raines, G.L., Miller, R.J., and Wentworth, C.M., 2000, GIS Data for the Geologic Map of California, California Department of Conservation, Division of Mines and Geology, CD-ROM 2000-07, scale 1:750,000. rule_notes: first match over major lithologies, then name, then description; volcanic with bottom age >= 145.0 Ma -> greenstone_metavolcanic; clastic sedimentary with bottom age <= 2.58 Ma -> alluvium; 'water' -> other
